report.summary: The one failing test, test_added_book_is_listed[chromium], is flaky, and the root cause is in the app: list_books() in app/main.py serves a per-user cache with no invalidation on add or delete, so the page often renders the pre-add (empty) list. Fix the app first by invalidating or removing that cache in insert_book and delete, then rerun the UI tests; the test itself is correct.

causes.title: Book list served from a random, never-invalidated cache after adding a book
causes.explanation: list_books() (app/main.py:151-157) returns the cached _recent_lists[user_id] with probability 0.7 whenever the user already has a cache entry, and it is only refreshed from the database on the other 30% of calls. insert_book() (app/main.py:160-167) and books_delete() (app/main.py:343-350) never update or clear _recent_lists. In this test the user opens /books first, which caches an empty list. After books.add(), the redirect to /books re-renders from that cache about 70% of the time, so the new row is missing and the page shows 'No books yet.' The other 30% of runs render the correct list, so the same code can pass on a rerun. The app's cache is the real defect, which is why this is classed as flaky rather than a test bug: the test's assertion and locator are correct. The randomness lives in the app, so the test's wait does not help. The same stale-cache defect affects any test that adds or deletes a book after the list has been read, so other UI tests may also flake even though they passed in this run.
evidence: Failure: 'Locator expected to contain text 'Frank Herbert'' / 'Actual value: None' / 'Error: element(s) not found' waiting for get_by_test_id("book-row").filter(has_text="Dune-640ffbd6")' (tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:15)
Aria snapshot of the failing page ends with: 'paragraph: No books yet.' The book was submitted (books.add) but is not rendered.
app/main.py:152: 'if user_id in _recent_lists and random.random() < 0.7:' then 'return _recent_lists[user_id]' (stale cache hit)
app/main.py:148: '_recent_lists: dict[int, list[dict]] = {}' is module-level, and nothing ever clears it
app/main.py:160-167 insert_book() writes to the DB without touching _recent_lists
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:9-15: the test opens /books, calls books.add(unique title, 'Frank Herbert', '1965'), then expects row(title) to contain 'Frank Herbert'. Nothing in the test is wrong.

Only one test failed in this run and no errors were reported, so the evidence for the exact failure rate is a single run; the probability figure comes from the code (random.random() < 0.7), not from run history.
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py, stop serving stale data. Simplest: delete the _recent_lists cache and always query the DB in list_books(). If caching is needed, invalidate _recent_lists[user_id] in insert_book(), books_delete() and api_update_book()/api_delete_book(), and remove the random.random() shortcut. As a test-side mitigation, nothing in tests should be changed for this; it would only hide the product defect.
